facts.text: Hebo lies within the traditional territories of the Tillamook people, a Salish-speaking tribe that inhabited the northern Oregon coast for over twelve thousand years.
Pioneers first settled the Hebo area in the late nineteenth century, drawn by opportunities in farming, dairy production, and lumbering.
Mount Hebo rises sharply to over three thousand feet, offering panoramic views of the Pacific Ocean and inland valleys.
Much of the land surrounding Hebo is public land managed by the expansive Siuslaw National Forest.
Roosevelt elk and black bears inhabit the forested uplands of Hebo, while the Nestucca River supports vital salmon runs.
Annual rainfall in Hebo averages approximately seventy-six inches, supporting lush vegetation and frequent coastal fog.
